data.title: Minister of Energy and Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources Holds Meeting with Japan's Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry
data.content:
Riyadh, November 20, 2026, SPA -- Minister of Energy and Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman bin Abdulaziz and Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry of Japan Akazawa Ryosei held a virtual meeting on November 9, 2026.
    During the meeting, the two ministers reaffirmed the strong and longstanding strategic partnership between Japan and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and discussed ways to further strengthen bilateral cooperation, particularly in the energy sector.
    Following discussions within the joint task force established in May 2026, the two countries confirmed the following:
    -The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia regards Japan as a strategic partner and attaches great importance to supporting Japan's long term energy security through reliable and stable crude oil supplies.
    -Japan expressed its deep appreciation to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for its stable and reliable supply of crude oil.
    -The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has already begun to replenish the joint oil stockpiling tanks in Japan.
    -Recognizing the longstanding importance of the Joint Crude Oil Stockpiling Project since its establishment in 2010 and the effectiveness it recently demonstrated, Japan intends to lend the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia crude oil storage capacity of 16 million barrels, alongside the existing 8 million barrels storage, using Japan's national stockpiling facilities on a time-bound basis.
    -Japan intends to purchase up to 8 million barrels of crude oil from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for its national stockpile reserves, subject to favorable market conditions and the completion of necessary internal procedures.
    -Japan and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia will cooperate under “POWERR Asia”, announced by Japan, to enhance energy security in Asia, based on the AZEC Ministerial Work Programme for Strengthening Oil Stockpiling presented at the AZEC Ministerial Meeting held on October 8. The Work Programme outlines future measures, including the development of both institutional frameworks and infrastructure for oil stockpiling in Asia, cooperation with oil-producing countries, and coordinated emergency responses.
    The two ministers welcomed the continued engagement between the two countries and expressed their shared aspiration to further strengthen the strategic energy partnership between Japan and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Both ministries will continue their constructive engagement to explore further energy cooperation and avenues for further enhancing the existing joint crude oil stockpiling scheme and maximizing its potential.
    -- SPA
